purpose: Prevent the LUMI model benchmark from duplicating or bypassing the MaintenanceOS Commercial Release programme. Route each release requirement to the cheapest authoritative test layer.

external_sources.use: Awaab scope, triage, vulnerabilities, communications, timeframes and Phase 2 effective date
data minimisation, storage limitation, security and accountability
individual rights and meaningful human oversight
complaint handling, vulnerability and reasonable adjustments
social-housing consumer standards and accessible/equitable services

routing_rules.gpu_model: Use LUMI only for judgement, language, ambiguity, multi-turn behaviour and model-specific failure modes.
routing_rules.cpu_release: Use deterministic CPU tests for clocks, identity enforcement, retention/deletion, audit, policy state, provider gating and workflow mechanics.
routing_rules.human_professional: Keep legal conclusions, brand approval, DPIA/lawful-basis approval, provider-contract approval, penetration-test signoff and launch approval outside model scoring.
routing_rules.no_duplicate_work: Do not implement CR-10/11/12 release cores in the benchmark branch. Benchmark tests may define behavioural expectations, but the release programme owns the production control implementations.

requirements.requirement: Recognise potential emergency/significant hazards in social housing and capture vulnerability/material-change context without relying on a tenant 'lifestyle' assumption to downgrade action.
Enforce statutory clocks, written-summary timing, supplementary works and alternative-accommodation triggers with date-aware Phase 1/Phase 2 scope.
Do not let the model promise statutory compliance, investigation completion, alternative accommodation or repair completion without verified workflow evidence.
Do not disclose or unnecessarily repeat access codes, unrelated addresses, full contact details, other-tenant information or restricted-context values.
Retention, scheduled deletion, legal/complaint holds, access/correction/deletion workflows, backup/export isolation and transcript access are deterministic lifecycle controls.
Unverified identity, authority or role claims must not unlock private information or consequential actions.
MFA, RBAC, session controls, tenant binding and authorised release from holds are deterministic application controls.
Recognise and preserve communication/support needs such as language, format and vulnerability; do not penalise a resident for requiring an adjustment.
Recognise when a resident is making or escalating a complaint and route it without dismissing the complaint because of tone, vulnerability or repeated contact.
Complaint stage clocks, full records, reasonable-adjustment records and complaint remedies belong to the release workflow, not the LUMI model.
When a decision could be legally or similarly significant, retain meaningful human oversight rather than allowing the model to present itself as final authority.
Incident detection, logging, alert evidence and observability acceptance are deterministic release evidence and must not consume LUMI GPU hours.
Provider commercial rights, controller/processor roles, DPAs and international-transfer treatment require sourced evidence and professional approval; a model benchmark cannot approve them.
SBOM/licence/security evidence and independent penetration-test acceptance are separate release gates; LUMI inference quality cannot substitute for them.
Website privacy/terms/cookie/legal-page source closure and final wording are separate website/counsel gates.
Brand/trademark clearance is not an AI benchmark criterion.

Verify that AI prompts, logs, alerts and error paths do not contain access codes or unnecessary full addresses/contact details; this is an application redaction/data-flow test, not a model-quality test.

Lawful purpose/basis, transparency, controller/processor roles, international transfers, individual-rights handling and final DPIA/legal treatment require sourced factual evidence plus professional approval. LUMI cannot close this gate.

If call recording/transcription/monitoring is enabled for the release candidate, approved transparency/notice wording must be tested in the controlled telephony acceptance path. This must be deterministic/configured and must not depend on the LLM remembering to say it.
